info.title: Niu Model & Inference API
info.description:
Model inference and management APIs for Niu. Browse the resource groups in the sidebar,
search by operation or path, and expand the request and response schemas for exact fields.

## Getting started
Use the [HTTP quickstart](/help/guides/api-quickstart/) for your first model request,
or the [JavaScript SDK guide](/help/guides/sdk-quickstart/) for typed clients.
[Download the complete OpenAPI 3.1 document](/docs/openapi/public.json).

## Authentication and scope
Inference uses a workspace API key. Management operations require the member session,
platform authority or Provider membership stated by that operation. These credentials
are not interchangeable. See each operation's security scheme and access description.
Legacy `project` path segments refer to workspaces; legacy `provider` paths refer to Providers.

## Requests and responses
Send the documented Content-Type and use the declared request schema. Response status codes,
error bodies and pagination fields are operation-specific. Follow the returned cursor rather
than assuming a list is complete. Streaming operations document their event format separately.

Monetary amounts and large counters use the exact string representation in their schemas.
Preserve currency and rate units; Provider purchase rates and customer charges are separate.

## Writes and retries
Where an operation documents an idempotency key, retry an uncertain outcome with the same
key and identical input. Preserve expected revisions for configuration updates; reload after
a conflict. A timeout does not prove that a write or an upstream generation did not execute.
Read the individual operation's retry and reconciliation behavior before resubmitting.

post.summary: Receive a signed Stripe checkout notification
post.description: Server-to-server callback; no installation or workspace bearer token is required. Verifies the signature over the original request bytes before parsing JSON, then requires an existing merchant-bound order and its saved checkout session. Paid evidence must match the saved session, amount, currency and configured live mode. Settlement is idempotent. Creating a checkout or visiting its return URL does not credit a balance. Unsupported or unrelated events are rejected rather than silently acknowledged. Maximum request body: 262144 bytes.

A missing browser_token_login field on an older Gateway does not establish support. This response does not disclose identities, credentials or upstream merchant status, and is not proof of deployed HTTPS/browser acceptance. Response carries Cache-Control: no-store.

post.summary: Sign in with a secure HttpOnly member cookie
post.description: Requires the configured HTTPS Origin header. Uses the same password limits and durable throttling as bearer login. Sets __Host-niu_member_session with Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ and Max-Age=28800; no Domain. The response contains session metadata only, never the bearer token. When supplied, Sec-Fetch-Site must be a single same-origin value. All responses use Cache-Control no-store.

post.description: Available only when NIU_DEMO_LOGIN_EMAIL and NIU_DEMO_LOGIN_PASSWORD are explicitly configured. Requires the configured browser Origin. Verifies the existing account password with ordinary sign-in admission and revocation checks, then issues an HttpOnly browser session cookie. Credentials are never returned. Existing account permissions apply; no account is provisioned. Disabled demo sign-in returns 404. Responses are not cached.

post.summary: Use an existing user access token in the browser
post.description: Requires an explicit trusted same-origin Origin and a valid durable Operator session token. Installation credentials, inference keys, revoked sessions and expired sessions are refused. Sets the existing HttpOnly SameSite cookie to the original token without creating an identity or session, extending expiry, changing role/scope, or returning the token in JSON. Cookie lifetime is capped at the original remaining lifetime and eight hours; every subsequent request rechecks the original durable session. Requires configured browser authentication origin. Responses are not cached.

get.summary: Recover this API key's saved ingestion history
get.description: Returns at most fifty newest records ordered by consent creation time and identity. Follow next_cursor as before until null. History includes revoked, expired and completed records without changing consent, publishing source capabilities or contacting an upstream service. A cursor from another key is unavailable. Later inserts do not shift continuation pages.

post.summary: Observe accepted image status using its original account
post.description: Separate current GetAsset permission and the original API key are required. One outstanding observation per ingestion, sixty per rolling hour and four concurrent gateway reads. One fixed bounded GetAsset request validates asset identity, group, project and image type before persisting status. The worker survives disconnect; interrupted reads record failure. This does not repeat creation, download media or grant reusable-reference rights. A claimed read_id is never replayed; use GET to inspect its saved outcome.

post.summary: Inspect and temporarily retain one exact inline image
post.description: Active workspace inference key required. Every required image detector must have current workspace processing consent. Detector approval is obtained server-side; client verdicts, hashes and remote URLs are rejected. Saves encrypted approved bytes, never publishes a fetch token or dispatches an asset. Four preparations may run concurrently. Retention is 1 to 900 seconds, with separate workspace and installation storage ceilings. Maximum JSON body is 12 MiB plus 1024 bytes. No request-payload logging on this endpoint. The source ID is an internal API reference, not a display label. Missing inspection prerequisites fail before detector disclosure.

post.summary: Claim and dispatch one inspected image ingestion
post.description: Requires original source API key, current policy, detector terms and reviewed CreateAsset permission. A trusted configured HTTPS origin serves the exact inspected bytes using an expiring capability. Four uploads may run concurrently. The bounded worker survives client disconnect; its immutable accepted or uncertain outcome is persisted. Never automatically replay an uncertain upload. Acceptance does not mean asset readiness. No client-supplied source URL, destination override or credential is accepted.

put.summary: Consent to ingestion of one inspected image into one ordinary asset group
put.description: Requires the original source API key and current workspace policy. Repeating identical unexpired consent is idempotent; consent cannot be renewed or retargeted. The dispatch_available flag requires retained unexpired source bytes, unrevoked unclaimed consent, configured source origin and encryption; it is not an admission guarantee. Erasing the source disables dispatch without rewriting consent or accepted history. This endpoint neither claims nor dispatches an upload. Dispatch requires a configured public HTTPS source origin and separate admission checks.

post.x-niu-status: Basic chat is implemented for configured native provider routes. Local buffered_full output rules support single-choice plain text streaming: retain the real upstream stream until terminal evidence, inspect the complete bounded output, then emit compatible sanitized chunks. Required output withholding emits a guardrail_output_withheld SSE error without [DONE]; known executed usage remains billable. Text buffering is limited to 1 MiB and total stream bytes to 2 MiB, with four concurrent collectors per process. Output rules with tools or structured format remain unsupported. Observation-only plain-text streams preserve delivery and asynchronously record clear, matched or indeterminate without transforming output. Mandatory and observation rules compose across workspace/key scopes. Optional collection and inspection have separate bounded capacity; observation overload does not deny the request. Function tools, streaming tool deltas, and structured JSON are opt-in on OpenAI-compatible routes only. Niu validates tool-call shape and structured JSON against a valid self-contained schema; json_object output must be an object. Schema compilation is offline and limited to 64 KiB, 4096 JSON nodes and depth 32, with bounded regular expressions. Niu does not execute tools. Structured JSON streaming validates assembled output before releasing [DONE], with a 1 MiB total content/refusal bound and at most 128 choices. Partial deltas are provisional; invalid final output sends an upstream_invalid_response SSE error without [DONE], while reported terminal usage remains accounting evidence. Token-priced routes support function calls and text-only tool-result conversations under the same input/output rates. Serialized messages, tool definitions, tool choices and response-format instructions count toward the configured input byte guard. Hosted tools and additional billable modalities remain unsupported. Chat pools allow at most one different-credential successor after a canonical OpenRouter immediate HTTP 401 with durable nonexecution and released holds, preserving operation price and funding under one deadline. Other errors and streams already returned to the client are not retried.

Tool definitions are limited to name, description and bounded offline object input_schema. tool_choice supports auto/any/none/tool and optional disable_parallel_tool_use. History requires uniquely identified assistant tool_use blocks followed immediately by matching user tool_result blocks with string content, before ordinary user text. Tools must remain declared for tool history. Streaming tools additionally require supports_messages_streaming_tools, supports_messages_tools and supports_messages_streaming; pools filter all required capabilities. Only sequential content blocks are supported; interleaved tool blocks fail safely. Native input_json_delta fragments are bounded to 64 KiB per tool and 256 KiB per message, parsed and schema-validated before content_block_stop is emitted. Tool IDs must be unique. Consumers must wait for message_stop before executing tool calls; error events and incomplete streams do not establish valid completion. Tool names, IDs and arguments are validated and projected; Niu does not execute tools. Required text input/output inspection rejects tool requests before dispatch rather than silently skipping tool content. A tool_use stop is a completed provider turn, not completion of a client task. Only version 2023-06-01 is supported (also used when omitted). Native input_tokens excludes cache reads/writes; total input accounting requires all three input categories plus output_tokens. Missing or null categories leave usage unresolved and reservations retained. Separate reasoning rates in the bound base price or a reachable context tier are rejected atomically before dispatch with 422 and x-niu-error-code unsupported_token_pricing; this adapter cannot report reasoning usage. Returned usage is not proof of a settled charge. Upstream commercial metadata is never forwarded. Native SDK and Claude Code compatibility are unverified. Streaming additionally requires supports_messages_streaming. Route pools filter this capability before priority/weight selection; no eligible candidate returns 503 before dispatch. Native SSE validates ordered text and opted-in tool events and projects customer-safe fields with a 64 KiB per-event limit. Completion requires message_stop; missing terminal evidence, upstream interruption and client cancellation retain uncertainty and reservations. Cumulative usage updates replace earlier counts; never sum deltas or infer missing categories. HTTP 200 alone is not completed usage. No credential switch or inference retry after headers. Required output inspection rejects streaming before dispatch. SDK messages.stream() stops at message_stop; an upstream extra [DONE] is not forwarded.

post.summary: Create a text response
post.description: The route must be an OpenAI-compatible provider route with supports_responses enabled. This public subset accepts a single text input and optional text instructions, output limit, sampling values, metadata and user identifier. Text streaming returns Responses SSE events and preserves terminal reported usage. Local buffered_full output rules retain real text streams until a validated terminal response and complete inspection, then emit compatible filtered lifecycle events. Withheld output emits a safe guardrail_output_withheld SSE error without a successful terminal event; known execution is still charged. Complete text and total input stream bounds are 1 MiB and 2 MiB, with four concurrent collectors per process. Observation-only text streaming preserves delivery and asynchronously records clear, matched or indeterminate without transforming output. Required and observation rules can compose across workspace/key policies; optional collection/inspection pressure does not block the request. Each Responses event is bounded to 16 MiB of UTF-8 bytes because terminal events repeat the full output; Chat events retain their separate 64 KiB bound. Oversized or malformed events fail the stream without inventing usage. Multimodal input, tools, prior-response state and other fields are rejected. HTTP 200 at stream start does not establish completion; inspect the terminal response event. Workspace model grants, source policy, rate/concurrency/token limits and configured billing apply. Canonical OpenRouter pools permit at most one different-credential successor after an immediate authentication refusal with durable nonexecution, released holds and no prior charge. The operation retains its original tariff, funding and shared deadline under a Responses-specific retry policy. No retry follows uncertainty or a stream already returned to the client.
